issues.title: [megatron] feat: add DeepSeek-V4-Flash SFT example (Megatron-Bridge backend)
issues.body:
### Summary

Adds a GSM8K SFT example for DeepSeek-V4-Flash via the Megatron-Bridge backend, mirroring `examples/sft/gsm8k/run_mimo_7b_mtp_megatron.sh`. Runs at TP1/PP4/EP8 (32 GPU), THD packed sequences, MTP enabled, unfused mHC/RoPE (`apply_rope_fusion=False`, `use_fused_mhc=False`), `use_mbridge=True, vanilla_mbridge=False`.

Folds in a 2-line fix to `verl/models/mcore/mtp_patch.py` so the MTP postprocess monkeypatch tolerates extra kwargs (`padding_mask`) that current Megatron-Core's `GPTModel.forward` passes — required by `model.mtp.enable=True`. Supersedes the standalone #6596 (closed).

### Environment / image — please read first

DeepSeek-V4-Flash SFT needs a specific stack and **will not run on a stock verl install**. Required environment:

- **Base image:** `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.04-py3`
- **verl** — this PR (includes the `mtp_patch.py` fix)
- **Megatron-Bridge** (`megatron.bridge`) + **Megatron-Core** with the DSv4 hybrid attention and THD support — Megatron-Core PR NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5011 (open). The example script fetches both onto `PYTHONPATH`.
- **DSv4 kernels:** `fast_hadamard_transform` + `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` — the example script installs these.

**Reference Dockerfile that bakes the full environment:** https://gist.github.com/Meirtz/7e240c5489851ebf79a6edfd357a40b7

The example script also bootstraps the Megatron-side pieces and kernels at runtime, so a plain `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.04-py3` container is sufficient to run it.

### Not a duplicate

The DeepSeek-V4 GRPO path is #6473 (`examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron.sh`); this is the **SFT** counterpart under `examples/sft/gsm8k/`. Same Megatron-Bridge backend, different trainer.

### Test

The DSv4 SFT path through Megatron-Bridge (THD, MTP, the `apply_rope_fusion=False` / `use_fused_mhc=False` config) was validated end-to-end on 8×H100 with a 4-layer DSv4 proxy: training and validation loss decrease, no NaN. The full model (TP1/PP4/EP8) and this exact GSM8K configuration have not been run by me; the script mirrors the validated config and the existing megatron SFT example structure. CI cannot exercise it until the DSv4 kernels are in verl's CI image.

### AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude) and reviewed by the submitter.

issues.title: [model] fix: use the transformers 5 rotary API in the GLM-4V attention patch
issues.body:
### What does this PR do?

GLM-4V training dies at the first attention layer on every transformers version this repo
supports.

`glm4v_attn_forward` replaces `Glm4vTextAttention.forward` whenever `use_remove_padding` or
`ulysses_sp_size > 1` (`monkey_patch.py:473`), so this is the ordinary GLM-4V path, not a corner:

```python
from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
```

```
transformers 5.3.0
ImportError: cannot import name 'apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb'
             from 'transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v'
```

transformers 5.0 replaced `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin, mrope_section)` with
`apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)` and moved the sectioning into
`Glm4vTextRotaryEmbedding`, which reads `mrope_section` from `config.rope_parameters` and folds
it into cos/sin before the attention ever sees them. `Glm4vTextAttention.forward` upstream is
now just:

```python
cos, sin = position_embeddings
query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)
```

Absent in every supported version — `requirements.txt` asks for
`transformers>=5.5.3,!=5.6.0,<5.11`, and the extras pin 5.3.0 / 5.5.3:

| transformers | `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb` in `modeling_glm4v` |
| --- | --- |
| 4.57.1 | yes |
| 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.5.3, 5.10.4, 5.16.1 | no |

It came in with #5724 (`transformers upgrade to 5.3.0`), which updated the config-side
`rope_scaling` → `rope_parameters` migration a few lines above but not the function that moved
with it.

`qwen2_vl.py` uses the same call and is **not** affected: `modeling_qwen2_vl` still exports
`apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb`. Only GLM-4V was migrated.

### The change

Call the function upstream calls, and drop the `mrope_section` lookup that fed the old one.

That lookup was dead twice over — it reads `self.rope_scaling` or `self.rope_parameter` off the
**attention module**, and on transformers 5 the attention module has neither (the config
attribute is `rope_parameters`, plural, and lives on the config):

```
transformers 5.3.0, Glm4vTextAttention
  self.rope_scaling    -> <ABSENT>
  self.rope_parameter  -> <ABSENT>
```

so the `assert` under it would have fired had the import ever got that far.

Restoring the old function instead would be wrong, not just unavailable: the 4.x call expects
cos/sin with a leading 3-section dim, and applying it to what transformers 5 produces raises
`IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 1`. The sectioning genuinely
moved.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. No PR or issue mentions `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb` on this
      repo; the one hit, #2603, predates the 5.x upgrade and is closed.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

`tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py`, following the `on_cpu.py` convention so it runs in
`cpu_unit_tests.yml`. It builds a real `Glm4vTextAttention` and `Glm4vTextRotaryEmbedding`, runs
`glm4v_attn_forward` with the CUDA-only flash-attention call patched out, and asserts the q/k
reaching attention equal `apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)` — the same rotary upstream
applies — with KV repeated to the query head count. A second case records why the argument had
to go rather than be restored.

Load-bearing, run against a clean `origin/main` worktree in the same environment:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py          # origin/main
>       from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
E       ImportError: cannot import name 'apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb' ...
1 failed, 1 passed

$ pytest tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py          # this branch
2 passed

$ ruff check / ruff format --check                          # ruff 0.12.2, as pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed! / 2 files already formatted

$ python3 tests/special_sanity/check_license.py --directories .
exit 0
```

The flash-attention call itself is CUDA-only and unchanged by this PR, so it stays covered by
the existing GPU tests.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

One import and one call site in `verl/models/transformers/glm4v.py`; the `mrope_section`
derivation is removed with them.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [x] Add / update the documentation. Not applicable.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s).

issues.body: ### What does this PR do? > Add **concise** overview of what this PR aims to achieve or accomplish. Reference related GitHub issues and PRs that help with the review. Replace part of the implementation of the Qwen3-omni moe series models with high-performance NPU implementations. Meanwhile, when training with frameworks such as [verl-omni](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni), this patch can also take effect by default to improve training performance. Co-author: @zhihaofang1017 ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+state%3Aclosed+qwen3+omni+patch - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI) - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off` - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]` - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test` - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title. - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching` ### Test > For changes that can not be tested by CI (e.g., algorithm implementation, new model support), validate by experiment(s) and show results like training curve plots, evaluation results, etc. We conducted experiments on the Qwen3-omni-30B model using a total of 16rank 910B.
